meta.coordinates: [x, z] on the ground plane. +X = east, +Z = south, north = -Z (Godot convention). Heights are meters above local ground.
meta.season: summer, a clear morning after overnight rain
meta.setting: An ordinary family back garden: a house with a patio and back door to the south, an apple tree to the west, a lawn, a flower bed, a vegetable patch at the far (north) end, and a wooden fence around it all.

areas.name: Backpack Hollow
areas.role: Wake-up pocket, the far end of the garden. Movement and camera tutorial.
areas.story: The flattened grass where Amodu was hiding when he shrank. His school bag lies beside it, 150 m tall. Home is the house on the far side of the garden.

areas.name: Blade Forest
areas.role: Densest walkable grass. First scale reveal.
areas.story: Densest walkable grass. A dandelion towers over it, and another has gone to seed; the first ant trail.

areas.name: Flower Bed
areas.role: Wonder beat and the first climb: daisy heads to leap between.
areas.story: A corner gone wild with daisies, buttercups and clover in the apple tree's shade. Dew still beads on every petal; a lost marble; a dew-strung web.

areas.name: Capstone Shelter
areas.role: Meet Opigo and Opumie. First sign of civilization.
areas.story: An ant watch post under a bottle cap propped on three pebbles, overlooking the Bare Patch.

areas.name: Bare Patch
areas.role: Pill bug tutorial fight. Colony Gate.
areas.story: Dry, cracked soil where a planter stood all summer; its ring is still pressed into the earth. The ants' front door is the biggest crack.

areas.name: Hose Run
areas.story: The hose from the water butt leaks at its coupling; the mist makes a morning rainbow. The ants run a water station here.

areas.name: The Rut
areas.role: The colony's moat. No bridge in any level: the termites go round by the driveway kerb, and the south stays shut until the captured causeway opens it in Level 4.
areas.story: Night rain filled the tyre rut the car left in the grass, and hose runoff keeps it full.

areas.name: Windfall Roots
areas.story: Beyond the Great Root: windfall apples like boulders, a gnawed apple core, fallen leaves that crunch and give you away.

areas.name: Spider's Edge
areas.role: BOSS: Garden Wolf Spider. The last stretch before the patio.
areas.story: The damp corner where the apple root dives under the patio edge. A silk-lined burrow, trip lines across the only way to the trowel ramp.

boundaries.note: Timber edging of the vegetable patch. Sweetcorn towers behind it.
Concrete kerb of the driveway; the family car is parked on it.
The patio's 5 cm edge: an 18 m cliff of paving slabs. See "patio".
The apple tree's trunk base and drifts of fallen leaves.

barriers.note: Uncut tussock between the Great Root and the Rut; it reaches into the water so there's no dry strip. Impassable.
Closes the gap between the Rut's east shore and the driveway kerb; it reaches into the water so there's no dry strip. Impassable: the termites go round it along the kerb top (paths/termite_raid).

water.name: The Rut
water.note: Tyre rut flooded by rain and hose runoff: the colony's moat, no bridge. Swimmable (slow, tiring, no diving). The termite causeway crosses it in Level 3 (docs/narrative/map-plan.md).

paths.label: Chapter 1 route: wake to Colony Gate
Garden Patrol: Patrol Gate to the Rut's north shore (the south opens in Level 4)
Root tunnel (sealed in the graybox; opened from the south side later)

paths.note: M8: Akpuru's raiders march at dusk along the top of the driveway kerb (a dry road; insects follow edges), climb down a kerb stair of a few stones at [350, 120], then west along the Rut's north shore to the Colony Gate. Seen from the Capstone. NPC path only; the tussock stays a wall for the player.

Level 3: the termites' mud-and-carton causeway across the Rut, south shore to the war-plan shore. Captured at the end of Level 3, it opens the south in Level 4. Not built yet; the layout check treats it as the one way south.

landmarks.name: Amodu's school bag
landmarks.real: 42 x 30 x 15 cm, upright and slumped
landmarks.note: Tallest thing in the level. Zipper on the south face is a climb route. Player compass.

landmarks.name: Dandelion clock
landmarks.real: 20 cm, gone to seed; parachutes drift over the forest

landmarks.name: Crisp packet
landmarks.real: empty crisp packet, silver inside, a puddle of rain in it
landmarks.note: The Meshy crisp packet laid on its side, crumpled, torn-open end facing west toward the ants' road; abandoned ant rest stop.

landmarks.name: Lost marble
landmarks.note: Refracts the clover canopy. Lore item.

landmarks.name: Root Hall (quest hub)
landmarks.note: Entrance between two root buttresses at the trunk base. Sealed until after the colony.

landmarks.name: Capstone (bottle-cap roof)
landmarks.real: 26 mm bottle cap on three 1 cm pebbles

landmarks.name: Lookout blade
landmarks.note: Thread ladder to a lookout at 25 m.

landmarks.name: Bead shrine
landmarks.real: one red glass bead from a broken bracelet

landmarks.name: Planter ring
landmarks.note: Circular imprint of a paint-bucket planter in the red earth.

landmarks.name: Colony Gate
landmarks.real: 4 cm hair band as an arch over the crack

landmarks.name: Worm castings
landmarks.note: Mounds of worm castings; also at the 'also' positions.

landmarks.name: Patrol Gate
landmarks.note: Colony side exit under a pebble.

landmarks.name: Leaking coupling / Water Station
landmarks.note: Jet sprays up and west; mist radius ~45 m with rainbow.

landmarks.name: Termite forward camp
landmarks.note: Mud tubes. Only evidence in Ch 1, occupied in Ch 2.

landmarks.name: Windfall apple
landmarks.real: 8 cm apple, bruised, one side pecked open, buzzing with fruit flies

landmarks.name: Apple core
landmarks.real: 7 cm apple core, gnawed and browning

landmarks.name: Little windfall
landmarks.real: 3 cm unripe apple from the June drop

skyline.name: Apple tree
skyline.real: 35 cm trunk, first branches at 1.4 m
skyline.note: Broad canopy from 520 m up, radius ~1.5 km: shades the west half of the level. Apples drop; birds sit in it.

skyline.name: House
skyline.note: The family's house, south of the garden. Its north face (z = 640) holds the back door, reached across the patio.

skyline.name: Garden shed
skyline.note: Wooden shed at the far end of the garden, beside the water butt.

skyline.name: Water butt
skyline.note: Green rain barrel by the shed; the hose runs from its tap.

skyline.name: Washing line
skyline.note: Shirts and towels drying high overhead.

skyline.name: Family car
skyline.note: Parked on the driveway; its tyres made the Rut when it rolled onto the grass.

skyline.name: Sweetcorn
skyline.note: Tassels 720 m up at the far end of the garden.

skyline.name: Tomato plants
skyline.note: Staked tomato plants; red fruit the size of houses.

skyline.name: Compost heap
skyline.note: In the far corner, steaming: rot, fungus and things that live on them.

skyline.name: Garden fence
skyline.note: 1.8 m wooden fence panels on three sides; the house closes the south. A gate on the east side opens onto the driveway.

viewpoints.name: Backpack summit
viewpoints.note: On the ridge of the Meshy school bag (its grab handle rises to 148 m behind).

veg_bed.note: Raised vegetable beds at the far end of the garden: sweetcorn, tomatoes, beans.

far_lawn.note: Grass-top level of the rest of the lawn, seen from high up.

heavables.name: Fallen stone
heavables.note: M2 The Stakeout Camp: shaken down onto the ants' camp by the bully's stomping, with their kit under it. Far heavier than any team of ants can shift (push class); pushing it off is the first thing Amodu does for them (world/level_story.gd).

heavables_note: Loose props Amodu can lift (<= 2.6 m) or push (<= 5.5 m); see world/props/heavable.gd.

expedition.note: Phase 3c expedition slice (docs/PLAN.md), spawned by world/expedition/expedition.gd when lawn_level.gd runs in expedition mode. Pill bug stand-ins become live creatures from this list.

jobs.title: A big piece of food
jobs.brief: The workers found a big piece of food by the school bag, far too heavy for one ant. Bring it home before the sun goes down.

patio.note: The final stretch: paving slabs 18 m up (5 cm), the back step 54 m higher (15 cm), and the back door. Amodu climbs the trowel, crosses the slabs, walks up the leaning brush onto the step and crawls under the door: home.

trowel.note: A dropped trowel, face down: its handle end is bedded in the soil (from), and you walk up the handle and the back of the blade, whose tip rests on the slabs just past the edge (to).

brush.note: A hand brush leaning on the step: its handle is a ramp up.

door.note: The back door. Warm light shows through the gap under it (1.2 m, too low to walk): crawl through and you're home.

flowers_note: Flower Bed climb: stems are climbable, heads are platforms. D1-D4 rise 12/22/32/42 m within power-jump reach of each other.

tree_base.note: The apple tree's base, baked in Blender by tools/bake_tree_base.py into assets/world/tree_base.glb: a soil bank heaved up by the roots, the lower trunk, and Root Hall, the caves inside it. Points are [x, y, z] with absolute heights (the lawn is near 0). Tunnels are round tubes; chambers are ellipsoids with flat floors.

route.note: Level 1, The Road to the Kingdom (docs/GAMEPLAY.md), without words (world/route_guide.gd): one landmark per stage, each in sight of the last. A column of golden motes rises over the next one and a gold diamond marks it on the compass. Reaching a later stage skips ahead, except an "in_order" stage, which counts only once it's the next one.

stages.name: The ants' camp
stages.why: M2 The Stakeout Camp: the ants' camp by the pencil log.

stages.name: The crisp packet
stages.why: M3 The Cut Road: the ants' old rest stop, torn open, mud tubes over the trail; the ants hand Amodu an axe (world/level_story.gd).

stages.name: The top of the bag
stages.why: M4 Over the Top: the whole garden below, and seed puffs snagged there to glide down on.

stages.name: The dandelion
stages.why: 80 m of yellow over the Blade Forest; aphids and ladybirds on it.

stages.name: The daisy stair
stages.why: Leap up the daisy heads in the Flower Bed.

stages.name: Root Hall's door
stages.why: M6: an ancient ant door between the apple tree's roots, sealed with stone. Remember it.

stages.name: The orb web
stages.why: M7 Caught: past the orb web, on the ant road (the rescue is Stage 2).

stages.name: The Capstone lookout
stages.why: M8: from the lookout, Akpuru's army marching on the gate.

stages.name: The Colony Gate
stages.why: M8 The Shut Gate: sealed for the siege; dusk falls; the old way (world/level_story.gd).

stages.name: Root Hall
stages.why: M9 The Old Way: heave the door stone and go in. The end of Level 1.

story.note: Level 1's story beats that need places (world/level_story.gd). The door stone seals Root Hall's mouth until the Colony Gate shuts; then Amodu can heave it aside. Past "inside" (in the tunnel, below max_y) the level ends.

door_stone.note: Root Hall's door: the door_slab model standing on its edge across the tunnel mouth.

story.leads_note: Where Opumie leads while an objective is up (keyed by the step's done_on in world/lawn/missions.json): [x, z] points she walks, waiting for Amodu (characters/companion.gd lead_along). Mostly the west ant road.

camp_stone.name: Fallen stone
camp_stone.note: While the stone sits on the camp the ants push at it from these spots; it counts as freed once moved freed_after metres. "kit" is the ants' leaf-wrapped bundle under it (the kit_bundle model).

first_night.note: The First Night camp, in the Blade Forest on the way to the Flower Bed (moved from [-125, -200] so the route doesn't double back; decisions.md 2026-09-27). Not built yet.

puffs.note: Dandelion seed puffs snagged high up (world/props/seed_puff.gd): grab one and glide down. Each settles on the highest surface below from_height (default 400).

pickups.note: Off the route (east): the abandoned ant rest stop in the crisp packet. A reward for exploring.

choppables.note: Beat 2 (docs/GAMEPLAY.md): a fallen twig across the ant road north of the hollow, the first thing to chop with the axe. Off the route home. The Spider's Edge trip lines are choppable silk too (landmark trip_lines).

survival.note: Survival (player/survival.gd, world/lawn/dew_drops.gd): dew clusters beside the main routes and ant roads every route_spacing metres, plus scatter more anywhere dry; seeded. Food is the crumbs in heavables (kind crumb) and the fallen apples and core (landmarks). Shelters are where he can sleep (from 18:00 to sunrise): it skips the night and sets where he wakes. Night hunters come out at dusk from their homes and go back at dawn.

biomes.note: Each area's own plants and things lying about (world/lawn/garden_dressing.gd, after the user's Grounded references): scatter = [model, how many, [size range m], sink m, fade-out m]; landmarks = big lost things placed by hand, solid and climbable: [model, [x, z], size m, yaw].

tree_grounds.note: The ground round the apple tree west of the lawn (docs/narrative/map-plan.md, the tree grounds): built by world/lawn/tree_grounds.gd with its own terrain, which meets the lawn at x = -360 and the baked root bank round the trunk. Unmown: thin grass in the shade, last year's leaves, windfalls, puddles along the drip line.

areas.name: Leaf-Litter Moor
areas.note: Dry curled apple leaves in drifts: they crunch underfoot (a blackbird turns them over later).

areas.name: Windfall Orchard
areas.note: Apples lying where they dropped, most rotting into the leaves: food, and fruit flies.

areas.name: Sap Falls
areas.note: A wound in the bark on the north-west side; amber resin runs down it and hardens at its foot.

areas.name: The weavers' silk ladder
areas.note: Two silk ropes with rungs hung from the weavers' landing on the Old Bough, 140 m up, down to the bank: the way up.

areas.name: West Root Door
areas.note: A gap under a root flare into the Rootway, on the dry side. Sealed until the Rootway is dug (tools/bake_tree_base.py).

dressing.note: A pruned branch lying where it fell.

bough.name: The Old Bough
bough.note: A limb low on the west side, pruned off long ago (the piece lies below: the pruned branch in the dressing); the cut has healed over. The weavers' landing on its back with their silk ladder hung from it, and a water shoot springing up near the end. An orb weaver's web hangs above it (OrbWeaverLair).

wormways.note: The Wormways: earthworm burrows under the lawn (docs/SURVIVAL.md). Baked by tools/bake_wormways.py (Blender) into assets/world/wormways.glb, placed by world/wormways/wormways.gd. Points are [x, y, z], y absolute (the lawn is near 0). Entrances open in the lawn (holes in the ground's collision and mesh); they're plugged with old casts until the first rain washes them out. A 5 mm burrow is 1.8 m across here; the Great Worm's are 8 m.

shaft.name: The old shaft
shaft.note: The Great Worm's old way up, long since plugged by a stone. Heave the stone out and daylight falls into the lair.

chambers.name: The Midden
chambers.note: Where the worms drag leaves down to rot: leaf ends and slime.

chambers.name: Root Hollow
chambers.note: Under the Flower Bed: roots hang through the roof.

chambers.name: The Flint Seam
chambers.note: Stones bedded in the clay: flint.

chambers.name: The Great Worm's lair
chambers.note: Deep and wide, its walls slick; the Great Worm lives here.
